name: Zostel Manali
summary: A backpacker hostel in Old Manali, in the orchard village above the Manalsu stream, with dorm beds and private rooms, a garden café and the social atmosphere Zostel is known for. A good base for walkers on a tight budget.
body: Zostel is one of India's largest hostel chains, and its Manali property sits in Old Manali, the village of kath-kuni houses and apple orchards about 2 km above the Mall. That location matters: you can walk to the Manu temple, the Hadimba temple and the riverside cafés, and you are away from the traffic of the new town. Rooms range from mixed and female-only dorms to simple private doubles, and the common areas fill with travellers swapping notes on Kasol, Spiti and treks.

Expect shared bathrooms in the dorms, basic furnishings and a lively evening scene rather than quiet luxury. It suits students, solo travellers and couples who want company and low prices. In peak months, especially May, June and the New Year week, beds sell out, so book ahead on the official website. In winter, ask about heating, as Old Manali nights drop below freezing.
why: Walkable Old Manali location among orchards
Dorm beds for a fraction of hotel prices
Easy place to meet other travellers and share taxis
price_band: ₹600–1,200 a dorm bed; ₹2,000–4,000 a night for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Does Zostel Manali have female-only dorms?
faqs.a: Zostel properties usually offer female-only dorms alongside mixed dorms and private rooms. Availability varies by season, so select the room type when booking on the official website or app and confirm at check-in.

faqs.q: How far is Zostel Manali from the bus stand?
faqs.a: Old Manali is about 2–3 km from the Manali bus stand. An auto-rickshaw or taxi takes 10–15 minutes, though traffic in Old Manali's narrow lane can be slow in season. Walking takes about 35–40 minutes uphill.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Manali open in winter?
faqs.a: Hostels in Old Manali generally stay open in winter, but services and heating vary. Check on the official website or by phone before booking in January or February, and pack warm clothes for cold nights.

name: Zostel Bir
summary: A Zostel hostel in Bir, close to the paragliding landing fields and the Tibetan colony, with dorms, private rooms and a common area full of pilots, meditators and backpackers. Simple, friendly and good value.
body: Bir has become a long-stay base for paragliders, meditation students and remote workers, and Zostel's property here caters to all three. Dorm beds and private rooms are simple and clean, and the common spaces are where people arrange tandem flights, share taxis up to Billing and plan walks to monasteries. The hostel is within reach of the landing site, the colony cafés and the tea gardens, so you rarely need transport within Bir.

Like most Zostels, it is social rather than silent, though Bir itself is calmer than Manali or Kasol. Staff can help connect you with registered paragliding operators; always check the pilot's licence yourself. Book ahead for October and November weekends, which are peak flying season. In the monsoon, from mid-July to mid-September, flying stops and the hostel is quieter.
why: Near the landing fields and Tibetan colony
Easy to arrange flights and shared taxis
Low prices for long stays
price_band: ₹500–1,000 a dorm bed; ₹1,800–3,500 a night for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Can Zostel Bir book paragliding for me?
faqs.a: Hostel staff can usually connect you with local operators. Before paying, make sure the operator is registered with the tourism department and ask to see the pilot's licence and insurance details. Prices are typically ₹3,000–4,500 a flight.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Bir good for long stays?
faqs.a: Yes, many guests stay a week or more for meditation courses, flying lessons or work. Ask about longer-stay rates directly. Bir has cafés with Wi-Fi, but mobile data is more reliable than fixed connections.

faqs.q: How do I reach Zostel Bir?
faqs.a: Take an overnight Volvo from Delhi to Bir or Baijnath, then a local taxi or auto. From McLeodganj, Bir is about 2.5 hours by taxi. The hostel shares exact directions after booking.

name: HPTDC Hotel Kinner Kailash, Kalpa
image_query: Kalpa Kinnaur hotel Kinnaur Kailash view
summary: The state tourism corporation's hotel in Kalpa, with rooms and cottages facing the Kinnaur Kailash range, a restaurant serving Indian and Himachali food, and parking. Dependable and fairly priced; usually closed in deep winter.
body: HPTDC, the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation, runs this hotel in Kalpa village, with a main building designed in a style inspired by local architecture and separate cottages a short walk from reception. Rooms have attached bathrooms with hot water and look towards the Kinnaur Kailash range across the Sutlej. The restaurant serves Indian, Chinese and Himachali dishes, which matters in a village with few places to eat after dark.

Government hotels are not glamorous, and service can be slow, but they are reliable, well located and fairly priced, which is exactly what saver and comfort travellers need on a long Kinnaur road trip. Book on the HPTDC website and ask for a mountain-facing room. The hotel usually closes from around December to March because of snow and cold; check current status before you travel.
why: Kinnaur Kailash views from rooms and lawn
Reliable government booking and fair prices
On-site restaurant in a village with few options

faqs.q: Is HPTDC Kalpa open all year?
faqs.a: No. The hotel usually closes from about December to March because of extreme cold and snow. Opening dates vary with the weather each year, so check on the HPTDC website or by phone before planning a winter or early-spring trip.

faqs.q: Do rooms at HPTDC Kalpa face the Kinnaur Kailash?
faqs.a: Many rooms and the cottages have views of the range, but not all. Ask for a mountain-facing room when booking and again at check-in. The lawn has open views for everyone.

faqs.q: How do I book HPTDC Kinner Kailash?
faqs.a: Book online on the HPTDC website, through HPTDC booking offices in Delhi, Shimla and other cities, or by calling the hotel. Online booking shows current rates and room types. Carry ID for check-in.

name: HPTDC Hotel Castle, Naggar
summary: Stay inside the kath-kuni castle of the old Kullu rajas, traditionally dated to about 1460 and now run by HPTDC. Simple rooms, some with balconies over the Beas valley, a terrace restaurant and the Jagatipatt shrine in the courtyard.
body: Naggar Castle stands above the village with a long view up the Beas towards the peaks around Rohtang. Built in kath-kuni style, with alternating courses of deodar and stone, it survived the 1905 Kangra earthquake and has been run as a hotel by the state tourism corporation for decades. Half the building holds guest rooms; the courtyard, shrine, gallery and terrace are open to day visitors, so expect some foot traffic during the day.

Rooms are plain rather than plush, with old-fashioned furniture and fireplaces in some, but the experience is the point: you fall asleep in a 15th-century fort and wake to the valley in morning light. The restaurant serves Himachali and north Indian food. The Roerich estate is a short walk uphill. Valley-view rooms sell out first, especially in May, June and during Kullu Dussehra in October.
why: Sleep in a 15th-century kath-kuni castle
Balconies looking up the Beas valley
Walk to the Roerich estate and village temples

faqs.q: Are rooms in Naggar Castle luxurious?
faqs.a: No, they are simple heritage rooms with basic facilities, attached bathrooms and old furniture. The appeal is the building, the views and the history. Travellers expecting a resort may find them plain; ask for a valley-view room.

faqs.q: Can non-guests visit Naggar Castle?
faqs.a: Yes. Day visitors pay a small fee to see the courtyard, Jagatipatt shrine, gallery and terrace, and can eat at the restaurant. Guest corridors are private. Daytime can be busy in peak season; evenings are quiet.

faqs.q: How far is Naggar Castle from Manali?
faqs.a: About 21 km, or 45 minutes by road along the left bank of the Beas. Local buses between Manali and Kullu via Naggar also stop close to the castle. Parking near the castle is limited.

name: Chonor House
summary: A small Tibetan-style hotel on Temple Road in McLeodganj, built and run by the Norbulingka Institute, with rooms decorated with murals by Tibetan artists. Steps from the Tsuglagkhang temple and quieter than the main square.
body: Chonor House was built by the Norbulingka Institute, which trains Tibetan artists near Dharamshala, and the hotel showcases their work. Each room is decorated differently, with murals on Tibetan themes painted by Norbulingka artists, handwoven carpets and wooden furniture made in the institute's workshops. The building uses local stone and slate and sits on a slope among trees just off Temple Road, a short walk from the Dalai Lama's temple complex.

It is small, so book early, especially when public teachings are scheduled at the Tsuglagkhang. The restaurant serves Tibetan and Indian food, and the terraces look over the Kangra valley. It suits travellers who want character and a central location rather than resort facilities. Revenue supports the institute's work in keeping Tibetan arts alive.
why: Rooms painted by Norbulingka's Tibetan artists
Short walk to the Tsuglagkhang complex
Revenue supports Tibetan arts

faqs.q: Who runs Chonor House?
faqs.a: Chonor House was built by and is run by the Norbulingka Institute, which preserves Tibetan arts and crafts in exile. Rooms are decorated with work by the institute's artists, and the hotel supports its activities.

faqs.q: How far is Chonor House from the Dalai Lama temple?
faqs.a: A few minutes' walk. It is on Temple Road, close to the Tsuglagkhang complex and Namgyal Monastery. Cars can reach the area, but the last stretch is narrow; staff can help with luggage.

faqs.q: Is Chonor House good for families?
faqs.a: It works for couples and small families who want a quiet, characterful stay. It is not a resort, so there are no pools or play areas. Some rooms are larger; ask when booking.

name: Banjara Camp and Retreat, Sangla
summary: A riverside lodge in the Sangla valley, set in an apple orchard by the Baspa, with rooms in a stone-and-timber building, cottages and Swiss tents. The best-known comfort stay in the valley, and a calm base for Chitkul and Kamru.
body: Banjara Camps & Retreats opened its first property here in the 1990s, and the Sangla camp remains one of the most established places to stay in Kinnaur. It sits in an orchard beside the Baspa river, a short drive from Sangla bazaar, with snow peaks rising on both sides. Accommodation is in a two-storey building of local stone and wood, independent cottages in the same style and Swiss tents with attached bathrooms.

The atmosphere is deliberately simple: rooms have no TV, Wi-Fi is limited or absent, and the camp avoids plastic. Meals are served together, and staff arrange walks to Kamru, Batseri and Rakchham and day trips to Chitkul. It suits families, couples and older travellers who want comfort and good food in a remote valley. It usually operates in the main season and closes in deep winter; check current status before you travel.
why: Orchard setting on the Baspa river
Stone-and-timber rooms, cottages and tents
Guided walks to Kamru, Batseri and Chitkul
price_band: ₹8,000–14,000 a night for a double with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: Does the Banjara camp in Sangla have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Connectivity is deliberately limited, and rooms have no TV. Mobile signal in the Sangla valley is also patchy. Treat it as a chance to disconnect, and inform family before you go.

faqs.q: Is the Banjara camp open all year?
faqs.a: It operates mainly from spring to late autumn and usually closes in deep winter, when the valley is snowbound. Exact dates change with the weather. Check current status with the property before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is the Banjara camp from Chitkul?
faqs.a: Chitkul is roughly 25 km further up the valley, about an hour by road. The camp arranges day trips, or you can take the HRTC bus from Sangla. Sleep at Sangla first to acclimatise before Chitkul.

name: Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort, Shimla
summary: An Oberoi resort at Chharabra, about 13 km beyond Shimla at roughly 2,500 m, on the site of Lord Kitchener's former residence, surrounded by deodar and oak forest. Quiet, polished and one of the best hotels in the Himalaya.
body: Wildflower Hall stands on a ridge at Chharabra, above Mashobra, where Lord Kitchener, Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army in the early 1900s, had his country residence. The original building was later destroyed by fire, and the Oberoi group rebuilt the property as a resort in a style that recalls the colonial original. It is surrounded by cedar forest with long views over the ridges towards the snow peaks.

The resort is designed for staying in rather than rushing out: forest walks start at the gate, there is an Oberoi spa, and the restaurants serve Indian and international food. Shimla's Mall is about 40 minutes away by car for a day visit. Prices are high and rise further in summer and holiday weeks. Book directly on the Oberoi website for current rates and packages.
why: Forest setting at about 2,500 m with long Himalayan views
Oberoi service and spa
Calm escape from Shimla's crowds

faqs.q: How far is Wildflower Hall from Shimla?
faqs.a: About 13 km from Shimla's centre, at Chharabra beyond Mashobra, roughly 40 minutes by car depending on traffic at Dhalli. The resort can arrange transfers from Shimla, Chandigarh and the Kalka railway station.

faqs.q: Is Wildflower Hall good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of the most popular high-end honeymoon stays in north India, with forest walks, spa treatments and quiet rooms with views. Book early for May, June, October and the December holidays.

faqs.q: What is the history of Wildflower Hall?
faqs.a: The site was the country residence of Lord Kitchener when he commanded the Indian Army in the early 20th century. The old building was destroyed by fire, and the Oberoi group rebuilt it as a luxury resort that opened in the early 2000s.

name: The Oberoi Cecil, Shimla
summary: A restored late-19th-century hotel on Shimla's Mall at Chaura Maidan, with colonial interiors, valley-view rooms and Oberoi service. The best address for exploring Shimla on foot in comfort.
body: The Cecil has stood at the western end of the Mall since the British summer-capital era and is one of Shimla's oldest hotels. After a long restoration by the Oberoi group in the 1990s it reopened as a heritage luxury hotel, keeping its timber-panelled atrium, high ceilings and colonial character. Rooms face either the valley or the town, and the valley side looks out over forested ridges.

Its location is the main advantage over Wildflower Hall: you can walk along the Mall to the Ridge and Christ Church, or west to the Viceregal Lodge, without a car. The hotel has restaurants, a bar and Oberoi spa services. Because private vehicles are restricted on the Mall, the hotel arranges access and luggage transfers. It suits travellers who want Shimla's history at the door and a high standard of comfort.
why: Walkable Mall location near the Viceregal Lodge
Restored colonial interiors
Oberoi standard of service

faqs.q: Where exactly is The Oberoi Cecil?
faqs.a: At Chaura Maidan, at the western end of Shimla's Mall, about 1.5 km from Scandal Point and the Ridge and a similar distance from the Viceregal Lodge. Vehicle access is via a permitted route; the hotel guides arriving guests.

faqs.q: Is The Oberoi Cecil a heritage hotel?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of Shimla's oldest hotels, dating from the late 19th century, and was restored by the Oberoi group before reopening in the 1990s. Many original architectural features have been kept.

faqs.q: Should I choose the Cecil or Wildflower Hall?
faqs.a: Choose the Cecil if you want to walk Shimla's Mall, Ridge and heritage buildings. Choose Wildflower Hall for a forest retreat 13 km outside town. Our signature itineraries often combine two nights at each.

name: Span Resort and Spa
summary: A riverside resort on about 12 acres on the banks of the Beas near Katrain, south of Manali, with cottages, gardens, a pool and a spa. A calm, upmarket base for the Kullu valley away from Manali's traffic.
body: Span sits on the Kullu–Manali highway near Katrain, roughly 30 minutes south of Manali town, on a long stretch of the Beas with its own riverbank. Accommodation is spread across cottages and rooms in landscaped gardens among pine trees, many with views of the river and the forested slopes opposite. Its location, between Manali and Naggar, makes it a convenient base for both.

Facilities include a swimming pool, a spa and health club, and restaurants serving Indian and international dishes. It is one of the most established luxury resorts in the Kullu valley and is popular with families and honeymooners. In peak months, rates rise sharply; book directly with the resort for current prices. Keep children away from the riverbank, as the Beas is fast and cold.
why: Private stretch of the Beas riverbank
Pool, spa and large gardens
Quiet base between Manali and Naggar

faqs.q: How far is Span Resort from Manali?
faqs.a: It is near Katrain on the Kullu–Manali highway, roughly 30 minutes' drive south of Manali town, depending on traffic. Naggar is about 20–30 minutes away across the river.

faqs.q: Does Span Resort have a swimming pool?
faqs.a: Yes, the resort has a swimming pool along with a spa and health club. Pool timings and heating vary by season; confirm with the resort when booking, especially for spring and autumn stays.

faqs.q: Is Span Resort good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The large gardens, cottages and pool suit families, and it is away from Manali's traffic. Supervise children near the riverbank, as the Beas is fast-flowing all year.
